$comment: Single source of truth for the Kotlin<->TS metric contract. The Kotlin engine plugin (engine-plugins/cibseven-history-metrics) emits Micrometer meters with these dotted names (otelName - also the OTLP wire name on the push path); the Prometheus normalisation (dots -> underscores, unit suffix `_milliseconds` for unit `ms`, `_total` for monotonic counters) yields promName - identically via the OTEL Collector's Prometheus exporter and via Micrometer's own Prometheus registry - which is what the TS queries (packages/connectors/analytics/analytics-client/src/metric-names.ts), the alert rules (playground/docker/prometheus/alerts.yml) and the Grafana dashboards (playground/docker/grafana/dashboards/*.json) consume. Histograms list the base promName; the `_sum`/`_count`/`_bucket` series are implied. `knownValues` documents label values consumers may rely on. Change a metric HERE first - contract tests on both sides (src/metrics-contract.test.ts, src/metrics-contract-labels.test.ts and MetricsContractTest.kt) enforce consistency. Reading rules every consumer follows (the TS tests check queries, alert rules and dashboards): (1) Durations are whole milliseconds: Micrometer rounds an observation UP to a whole base unit before it picks the bucket, so seconds would empty every sub-second bucket. `buckets` are the explicit bucket bounds in ms the plugin registers. (2) A counter or histogram series is created on its first event, and increase()/rate() never count a series' first sample, so a rare event (the first incident of a type at an activity) would read 0. Read them only as `(increase(X[R]) and present_over_time(X[1h] offset R)) or (max_over_time(X[R]) unless present_over_time(X[1h] offset R))`: a series without a sample in the hour before the window started was born inside it, and its value is the window's count (`increaseIn` in src/queries/helpers.ts). Where the hour before the window lies past the retention, Prometheus deleted it and every series would pass for new: read plain increase() there. (3) Every gauge is an engine-wide figure from an engine query, reported alike by every node of a clustered engine: read it as `max by (<its labels>)(gauge)` before any further aggregation, never a plain sum over nodes. (4) Counters count per node, so every node of an engine exports as its own series: on the OTLP path set a unique `service.instance.id` per node (the Collector's exporter keys series by it), on the Actuator scrape path the target's `instance` label does it.
